clue.text: Letter written for a piastre perhaps

definitions.note: the letter H, sounded as a breath, is the classic example

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of 'a piastre' could be set out in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note about the value of a Middle Eastern coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A PIASTRE. The definition is a noun: an aspirate is a letter such as H, said with a puff of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics an aspirate is a breathed sound, and the letter H is the standard instance.

clue.text: Having a certain leaning

parts.note: reads like a political bias or opinion, but describes something physically tilted

explanation.definitionFit: Something on a slant leans in one particular direction, literally rather than in its views.

clue.text: A vendor of fruit taking in five hundred pounds

indicators.note: the fruit word swallows the other letters, as if accepting them inside

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
D is the Roman numeral for 500
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A fruit seller takes £500 in a day's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling seller of small goods, so a vendor.

clue.text: Ordered beer at a discount

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged differently, so the letters of 'beer at' are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone buys beer cheaply in a happy hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like asking a barman for a drink; it rearranges BEER AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money returned or knocked off the price, a reduction.

clue.text: Call in a friend at last

parts.note: to call something by a name is to term it
an ally is a friend on your side

explanation.surface: Someone finally phones a pal for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call in' reads as a summons, but CALL gives TERM and IN stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminally means at the end, finally; 'at last' carries the same sense of conclusion.

clue.text: A French lie causing disquiet

parts.note: un is the French word for 'a'
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A falsehood from France stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' suggests a falsehood but means to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is a state of agitation or discontent, as is disquiet.

clue.text: Another will complete the score

parts.note: reads like a sporting result, but a score is twenty and one more number added makes it up

explanation.definitionFit: A score means twenty, so the number one short of it needs one more to reach that total.

clue.text: Dicky the Elder, an early English king

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters of 'the Elder' are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old man with a weak heart turns out to be an Anglo-Saxon monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name (Richard) beside 'the Elder', but is the anagram signal on THE ELDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred was the name of Anglo-Saxon kings, notably Ethelred the Unready, before the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Irascibility is sent up among seamen

indicators.note: among says one piece goes in the middle of the sailors' word

parts.note: tars is an old word for sailors

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Bad temper is ridiculed by the sailors on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down clue: the word read upwards gives TNES. 'Irascibility' is the definition; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartness is sharpness of manner or temper, close to a quick-tempered irritability.

clue.text: Hen-red with black spots!

parts.note: the beetle is red with black spots

explanation.definitionFit: The small beetle is red with black spots, and split in two its name means a female bird, a hen.

clue.text: Basic security for sailors

parts.note: sounds like a pension or insurance scheme, but means what holds a ship in place

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's heavy hook dropped to the seabed keeps the vessel steady, its fundamental safety at rest.

clue.text: Flat round insect that's a nuisance on the lawn

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: plain land is flat
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A creature crawling around flat ground pesters gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat round' reads as a description of a squashed object, but 'round' is the container signal. Plantain is a common lawn weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a broad-leaved weed that spreads across grass and annoys gardeners.

clue.text: Many returned bearings wrongly obtained

indicators.note: returned means the word for many is read back to front

parts.note: lots means many
E and N are compass bearings, east and north

explanation.surface: Lots of compasses brought back were acquired by theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods are taken by theft, so obtained dishonestly.

clue.text: Indicating a need for quiet or nursing

parts.note: p (piano) means quiet in music
tending the sick is nursing them

explanation.surface: A patient signals they need peace or medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signal or foreshadow, so indicating something to come.

clue.text: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people

definitions.text: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people

parts.words: Their rise and fall may well be of interest to outgoing people
parts.note: outgoing suggests sociable, but means people going out who check the weather instruments

explanation.definitionFit: Pressure gauges forecast the weather by rising and falling, useful to anyone heading out of doors.

clue.text: The strength of the current

parts.note: reads as the force of a river or tide, but means electrical current

explanation.definitionFit: Electric current is measured in amps, and the amount flowing is its measure in those units.

clue.text: Feeling it's modish to be frugal with about a hundred

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: about means the frugal word goes round the letter for a hundred

parts.note: to stint is to be sparing
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A gut sense that it's stylish to be thrifty with around a hundred pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an innate sense or intuition, a gut feeling.

clue.text: A couple of pence increase in value

parts.note: p is pence, and two of them give PP
a raise is an increase, as in pay

explanation.surface: A tiny rise in what something is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of, so to value.

clue.text: Originally put a male in control

indicators.note: done originally means done in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man was first installed to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like 'at first' and invites a first letter; it rearranges PUT A MALE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate is to handle or steer cleverly, to control.

clue.text: Go over fault

definitions.meaning: to switch to the other side

explanation.definitionFit: To go over to the enemy side is to desert, and a flaw is an imperfection.

clue.text: To withstand broken rest is S essential

indicators.note: broken means the letters of 'rest is' are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Interrupted sleep is vital to holding out.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or hold out, as to withstand does.

clue.text: Serve a non-drinker, getting a tip

parts.note: TT means teetotal
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A waiter serves a teetotaller and gets a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity; it means END. TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend on someone is to wait on or serve them.

clue.text: Complete little book in the country

indicators.note: in places the book's abbreviation inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT, short for New Testament, is a book of the Bible shortened

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a short book while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Share curiosity

definitions.meaning: a stake or part ownership in a business

explanation.definitionFit: A stake in a company is a holding in it, and inquisitiveness is attention drawn to something.

clue.text: A loose relation

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A family member with free-and-easy ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective describing the relation, but is a verb meaning UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is a parent's sister, a relative.

clue.text: Appreciate sage as well!

parts.note: to like is to appreciate
sage means wise

explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb; it is the adjective meaning WISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means also, in the same way.

clue.text: A course in evergreen tree shaping

indicators.note: in says the meal course sits inside the words 'evergreen tree'

explanation.walkthrough: 'shaping' is a link word here, suggesting the hidden letters form a part of the tree words.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served in a meal, a main or intermediate course.

clue.text: Calm converse

parts.note: reads as peaceful conversation, but means the opposite of calm

explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and flustered is the reverse state to being serene.
